verdict.rationale: Obsidian's own docs say vaults are local plain-text Markdown files that work offline with no sign-up, so it runs fully without the vendor's cloud. Users who de-Googled or left Roam confirm they own their files locally. Multi-device sync without Obsidian Sync relies on third-party services such as Git, Dropbox or iCloud, and one user reports Android save timing can break git syncing. Missing for 10: a first-party self-hostable sync backend, documented guidance for running user-operated sync reliably.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the whole system without the vendor's cloud — local-only mode or a self-hosted sync backend I operate myself

citations.quote: Obsidian uses non-proprietary plain text Markdown files stored locally on your device. You have total control over your data, which means you can use Obsidian offline
Free without limits. No sign-up required.
Obsidian syncs with Obsidian Sync, Dropbox, iCloud, OneDrive, Git, and many other third-party services.
Because notes are plain text files, you can use other text editors and file managers to edit and manage notes.
